sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Coral Gables
sections.html:
Most Gables owners end up choosing between a broker listing, a sale handled on their own, and an as-is offer from a cash buyer. How fast you need the money and what shape the house is in usually settle it.

One local wrinkle: more than 1,000 properties sit on the Coral Gables Register of Historic Places. If your address might be one of them, ask the city before you promise a buyer any renovation. At $2,373 a month, typical rent is high enough that some owners wonder about keeping the house as a rental, but that brings landlord duties of its own.

Coral Gables is a Miami-Dade County city of 49,578 people, and owners live in 64.5% of its homes. The typical owned home is worth $1,089,900, so a pricing opinion on your own block matters more than any citywide number.

Many buyers come from abroad or from out of state. A translated summary of your sale terms can head off confusion at the table, and so can a tidy title file, because those buyers usually want a quick, clean closing.

The city's permits page lists every permit it issues, and the City Services Directory covers anything you cannot find there. Ask the building staff whether any permit tied to your address is still open. It is better to learn that now than when a buyer's title agent asks.

The Development and City Projects page tracks traffic calming and large construction, so look at it for work planned near your block. Meeting agendas and public notices are posted under City Meetings if you want to see what is coming.

In Miami-Dade the deed tax runs 60 cents on each $100. The county also levies a 45 cents per $100 surtax, yet a transfer that moves only a single-family home does not owe it. The base rate sits in s. 201.02, and every signer on the deed is on the hook for it, whatever the contract says.

  • Payment goes to the clerk at the moment the deed is filed.
  • Under section 28.24 the first page costs $5.00 and later pages $4.00, with trust fund and technology charges added.
  • Section 689.01 asks for two witnesses to sign the deed.

Ask the title agent for an itemized closing statement so you can see each charge before you sign.

Someone buying a Gables homestead you have held for decades can face a much bigger bill than yours, since the sale pushes assessed value up to just value.

  • Save Our Homes holds yearly growth to the lower of 3 percent or inflation.
  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off taxable value. Claim it by March 1.
  • Renting the house out ends it.

The appraiser does not mail bills. The tax collector does, and the discount starts at 4 percent for a November payment. For questions about an assessment, call the Miami-Dade appraiser's public line at 305-375-4712.

sections.h2: If the house has a mortgage default, a tenant or an estate
sections.html:
Three situations, three separate timetables. After final judgment in a foreclosure the court auction lands 20 to 35 days out, so a private closing ahead of it can protect what equity you have. When an estate sells, the personal representative's deed is listed as non-taxable.

  • Estates of $150,000 or less in non-exempt property may use summary administration under s. 735.201.
  • Section 83.57 requires 30 days' notice to end a monthly tenancy.
  • Unpaid rent starts with a 3-day written demand.

The Clerk of Court offers a free alert that flags any deed or mortgage recorded under your name. That is handy for an empty or inherited house.

sections.h2: Steps after you accept an offer
sections.html:
Once you accept, the deed gets drafted, signed before two witnesses and recorded with the Miami-Dade clerk. Witnessing by audio-video is allowed, so an owner living in another state can still sign.

  1. Gather mortgage payoff information and any open permit records.
  2. Confirm whether your homestead ends with the sale.
  3. Ask the title agent how the year's tax bill will be divided.
  4. Read the settlement statement line by line before closing day.
  5. Keep a copy of the recorded deed.

If you are buying another Florida home, file the portability form with the new homestead application.

Relief for older owners and for veteran owners rides on the homestead, which means a sale ends it for that house. The Miami-Dade appraiser lets owners file widow and veteran disability exemptions online.

  • A veteran past 65 with a lasting service-connected disability may get a homestead discount that matches the VA rating.
  • Deferral requests go to the tax collector by March 31.

If you hold one of these benefits, ask the appraiser what happens to it at closing and whether you can use it on the next home.

A buyer paying cash does not need a lender's appraisal, so there is no loan approval to wait on and no list of required repairs. You still need clear title, so any lien, unpaid code charge or open permit has to be paid or accounted for at the table.

That makes an as-is offer a fit for a house with deferred maintenance, a tenant in place, or an owner who is moving on a deadline. It is a poor fit if the house is in good shape and you can wait, because a retail buyer may pay more. Get at least two offers, and ask each buyer to show proof of funds and name a closing date in writing.

On closing day, bring photo ID and keys, garage openers and any warranty paperwork. The title company will walk you through where to sign, and the proceeds are sent by wire or check after the deed is recorded.

sections.h2: What to have ready before you talk to buyers
sections.html:
A little preparation shortens almost any sale. Pull your deed, your latest tax bill, the mortgage payoff figure and any permit paperwork into one folder. If you are working with heirs or co-owners, agree early on who has authority to sign.

Then compare offers on what you would actually net, the time to close and the chance the deal falls apart. A cash buyer can skip lender appraisals and repair demands, while a listing reaches more buyers but adds showings and loan conditions. Ask each buyer in writing who pays for title, recording and deed tax.

faqs.q: How much is a typical Coral Gables house worth?
faqs.a: The typical owned-home value is $1,089,900 for 2020-2024. Your own house could land well above or below that.

faqs.q: Does a historic designation affect my sale?
faqs.a: It can, if the house is on the city's historic register. Ask city staff about your address before you promise a buyer any renovation.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamp tax on a Coral Gables deed?
faqs.a: Whoever the contract names, though everyone on the deed shares liability. The surtax skips a document moving only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: Will my property taxes follow me to a new home?
faqs.a: Partly. Portability can move some homestead savings to a new Florida home if you qualify, using Form DR-501T.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about my assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Miami-Dade appraiser's public line at 305-375-4712 or book an appointment through the appraiser's website.
